prompt: The client asks: "Should the city build a new bus line or improve existing routes?" Fact sheet: a new line costs $50M and would serve 8,000 riders a day; upgrading existing routes costs $20M and cuts trip times 20% for 40,000 riders a day; ridership fell 15% as trips slowed; city hall was renovated last year. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: For $20M, upgrades cut trip times 20% for 40,000 daily riders, against $50M for a new line serving 8,000, and slow trips are why ridership fell 15%. The main risk is that faster trips don't win riders back. Putting it together, improve the existing routes first.
options.feedback: The answer comes last. Lead with the recommendation, then support it.

On the other hand, there is the risk that faster trips don't win riders back. It depends on the client's priorities, so I'd want more analysis before committing either way.
